NDCG divides discounted gain at the predicted top k by the best possible top-k gain from all judged candidates. MRR uses the reciprocal rank of the first relevant result; this implementation reports MRR@k. Define whether zero-relevance queries are retained in the average; here they contribute zero. A truncated candidate list cannot reveal the ideal ranking of documents that were never supplied.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** $DCG@k=\sum_{r=1}^k(2^{rel_r}-1)/\log_2(r+1)$ and $NDCG=DCG/IDCG$ for positive ideal gain. MRR uses $1/r$ for the first relevant rank. State the gain convention and how queries without relevant items are handled; otherwise implementations can disagree while each follows a plausible definition. [3](https://nlp.stanford.edu/IR-book/)

For the implementation or system context discussed above, see [1](https://www.evidentlyai.com/ranking-metrics/ndcg-metric) and [2](https://www.evidentlyai.com/ranking-metrics/mean-reciprocal-rank-mrr).
